title: Amos Tversky and Daniel Kahneman — Loss Aversion in Riskless Choice: A Reference-Dependent Model (1991)
use: Reference-indexed preferences, loss aversion versus diminishing sensitivity, and alternative explanations of buying/selling discrepancies; original one-object specialization in this chapter.
verification: Inspected actual university-hosted primary paper PDF: introduction, section II (printed pp. 1046–1053) and section III opening (printed p. 1054). Read fixed-reference comparison, constant loss-aversion specialization and discussion of income effects/strategic behavior/transaction legitimacy. Did not reproduce the paper's empirical results or treat the chapter's lambda as an empirical estimate.

title: David Laibson — Golden Eggs and Hyperbolic Discounting (1997)

verification: Retrieved the PDF through the author's Harvard page and inspected section II, especially printed pp. 449–451 (equation 1, beta-delta weights and intrapersonal equilibrium). Earlier old URL timed out; this modern author-hosted PDF was successfully read. Historical institutional claims, calibration and saving-model conclusions are not imported.

title: Frank Schilbach — MIT 14.13, Lectures 3 and 4: Time Preferences (Theory), 10 and 12 February 2020

verification: Inspected official 65-slide PDF, especially slides 11–14, 40–51 and 61. The notes credit materials by Koszegi and Laibson and the O'Donoghue–Rabin framework; the chapter preserves that attribution. Chapter numbers and exercises are original. A separate scanned O'Donoghue–Rabin paper was not readable and is not claimed as an inspected source.

verification: Inspected actual dated v2 PDF sections 3.1–3.2 and the difference-in-means portion of 3.3, printed pp. 25–29 (PDF pp. 51–55).
